obtained.how: no full text: closed at Wiley/ESA and JSTOR, no repository or author copy found (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, web search; the Internet Archive holds only Ecology 1983's index and contents). The abstract was read via the OpenAlex API and the FAO AGRIS record

bibliography.note: Earl E. Werner, James F. Gilliam, Donald J. Hall, Gary G. Mittelbach (Dec 1983), Ecology 64(6): 1540–1548

claims.claim: small bluegill sheltering from bass in vegetation fed at about a third of the open-water rate and grew 27 % less
claims.note: Abstract only, so not confirmed. The abstract says the small class took a greater fraction of its diet in vegetation, 'where foraging return rates were only one-third of those in the more open habitats', and its growth increment was 27 % less. The one-third is the vegetation habitat's return rate relative to open habitat, not the fish's overall feeding rate, so 'fed at about a third of the open-water rate' overstates it; §3.7.1's wording is closer

claims.claim: at a cost of 27 % less growth in a divided-pond experiment (abstract)
claims.note: the abstract describes a 29-m divided pond, three bluegill size classes and eight largemouth bass on one side, and a 27 % smaller growth increment for the small class

claims.claim: small bluegill confined to vegetation by bass got about a third of the open-water foraging return and grew 27 % less (abstract only)
claims.note: matches the abstract's wording; the paper already flags it as abstract only

claims.claim: adults split their foraging time among foods in proportion to f⁴ (after Werner et al. 1983 and Wu & Culver 1992)
claims.note: a design choice 'after' the paper. The habitat-profitability results (habitat use that maximizes return rate) are in the companion paper: this paper's abstract cites it as 'Werner et al. 1983' for that point. See notes

claims.claim: fish sample the bed and settle where it pays, moving within days as returns shift; pond bluegill moved between the open water and the sediments within days as their profitability changed
claims.note: Probably mis-cited. The research note this came from (Real lake ecology for calibration/fish_zooplankton_coupling.md:525) credits it to Werner, Mittelbach, Hall & Gilliam 1983, a different paper; this paper's abstract does not mention it

notes: A second Werner et al. 1983 needs to be in the references. Crossref confirms the companion paper: Werner, E. E., Mittelbach, G. G., Hall, D. J. & Gilliam, J. F. 1983. Experimental tests of optimal habitat use in fish: the role of relative habitat profitability. Ecology 64(6): 1525–1539. doi:10.2307/1937507. The code's 'moved between open water and sediments within days' and §4.5's profitability-weighted allocation most likely belong to it (1983a/1983b). Other abstract-level details of this paper: each bass ate on average about one small bluegill every 3.8 d; the larger bluegill grew faster with bass present, because the small fish left the open habitats' resources to them.
